title: Layout lives in the markup
statement: A component MUST render its own structure: the rows, columns and slots its parts sit in. A stylesheet MUST NOT move an element into another element's box or restyle it from outside its component, so no `display: contents` and no `:has()`. When a control from further down belongs in a heading's row, the heading offers a slot and the control renders into it, as a section's header row holds its list's Expand all.
notes: Absolute positioning stays for marks and decorations inside a component's own box, such as a graph node's chevron.

title: Styles are set by class
statement: A style rule MUST select by class, attribute or ID. A selector that names only elements, such as `header`, MUST NOT be used outside the base styles, because it reaches every such element on every page, including ones added later. The base styles may set the page and its plain text and controls: `html`, `body`, headings, paragraphs, links, code, and form controls.

title: Colors and shadows are tokens
statement: A color, including a shadow's color and the backdrop behind drawers and dialogs, MUST be a custom property defined in `:root` (with its dark value in the dark theme), and every rule MUST use it through `var()`. Component inline styles MUST NOT set colors. A size several rules share, such as `--node-radius`, SHOULD be a token too.

title: Generic components know nothing of specs
statement: A component in `app/src/components` MUST import only React and other generic components, never the spec pages, the graph, the shell or the data types. What a spec page needs from it comes in through props, such as a list's items, its row renderer and its label.

title: Kind labels become plural only through plural() and lowercase only through lowerLabel()
statement: Code MUST make a kind's label plural with `plural()` from `app/src/plural.ts`, never by adding an "s", so every page and the graph say "Capabilities" and "Open questions" the same way. Inside a sentence a label MUST be lowercased with `lowerLabel()`, which keeps an acronym such as "UC requirement" whole, never with `toLowerCase()`.

title: Every control has an accessible name
statement: Every button, link and form control MUST have an accessible name: its text, an `aria-label`, or a label. An icon-only button names what it does ("Collapse LA-TRC-UC09"), and a control with a keyboard shortcut also states it in `aria-keyshortcuts`.

title: American spelling
statement: Code, UI text, specs and docs MUST use American spelling, such as modeling, color, center, behavior, organize and labeled. Fixed external names keep theirs, such as the HTML attribute `aria-labelledby`.

title: Every grid says its columns
statement: A CSS grid MUST declare `grid-template-columns`, and a single column MUST be `minmax(0, 1fr)`. A grid with no column template sizes its column to its widest content, so a long title or a wide list would widen the column past its panel and be cut off, instead of shrinking, wrapping or truncating. An icon grid that only centers one item (`place-items`) is exempt.

title: Themes only set tokens
statement: Every visual value (color, font, text size, density, radius, gap and motion speed) MUST come from a token in `:root`, so that a theme can change it. A theme MUST be data that sets those tokens and nothing else: its file names token names only, and the stylesheet written from it MUST have no selector but `:root` and set only custom properties. Every built-in theme MUST pass WCAG AA in both its light and dark sets: body text, muted text and the accent at least 4.5:1 on the page and on a sheet.

title: One address per thing
statement: A record's address MUST be its bare ID (`/LA-TRC-UC09`), a product's and a domain's included, and a group's MUST be its place in the graph's tree: a stage or folder under its domain (`/LA-EXP/define/use-cases`), or a record's group of one kind of child (`/<parent-id>/<kind>`). The app's own pages MUST be lowercase words (`/`, `/format`, `/settings/appearance`), so that no ID, which starts with a capital, can take their address; a space's Checks page is its product's ID and a word (`/LA/checks`). Every address of a record or group MUST be built by `addressOf` in `app/src/views/address.ts`, the one function that makes them: no other file MAY build such a path by hand. An address that changes form changes everywhere at once, with no redirect from the old one (`LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R20`).

title: Changes are hard cutovers
statement: When something is renamed or reshaped (an address, a function's signature, a command ID, a stored key, a class, a column or a label), every call site, record and test MUST move to the new form in the same change, and the old form MUST be deleted. The code MUST NOT keep redirects, aliases, second signatures, upgrades of saved state, or old names kept to avoid churn. Saved state in an old form is dropped: a stored entry that is not valid today is ignored, never converted.

title: Nothing outlives its purpose
statement: When a behavior is removed or replaced, everything that only served it MUST go in the same change: its code, exports, files and dependencies, its styles, its commands and icons, its tests and its records. The code MUST NOT keep a file, export or dependency nothing uses, a class selector nothing draws, a command nothing handles or nothing can reach, or an icon nothing shows. Every mark the Graph or the ERD stage can draw (a box's shape or fill, a badge, a line style) MUST be listed in that stage's key with what it means: a mark that can't be explained can't ship. Each of these is checked, so a leftover fails instead of surviving because nobody remembered it.

title: Everything clickable shows a hover state
statement: Anything the pointer can click (a card, a graph node, a row in a menu, a button) MUST change when the pointer is over it, and only clickable things MAY. Every hover uses the shared tokens in `:root`: `--hover-bg` tints rows and plain buttons, `--hover-ring` rings cards and graph nodes, and `--hover-speed` times the change, which reduced motion turns off. A card takes the ring anywhere on it, from its title stretched over it (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R14`). A graph node that is not clickable, such as the center or a file, keeps the default cursor and no hover.

title: The stage behind, panels floating over it, every panel edge resizes
statement: On a wide screen a focus page MUST read as one stage filling the window behind everything, with every other part floating over it as an inset, frosted panel: the navigation, the tab panel (the page bar and the header strip), the wiki card and the side bar, each a rounded box a gap (`--float-inset`) from the window and from each other, with a soft shadow. Frosted means a mostly opaque surface (`--float-dense`, about 82%, for the nav, the tab panel, the side bar and the chat, `--float-light`, about 72%, for the wiki card) over a strong backdrop blur (`--float-blur`, 22 px), the stage showing through as shape and color while text keeps WCAG 2.2 AA contrast; the surfaces are tokens with light and dark values, and under `prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce` every panel MUST be opaque. A page without a stage floats as one panel right of the nav. The inner edge of each resizable panel MUST be a `ResizeHandle` from `app/src/components/ResizeHandle.tsx`, the one component that draws a splitter, so each handle drags, steps with the arrow keys (Shift for bigger steps), jumps with Home and End, resets on double-click and is remembered alike. On a narrow screen the nav and the side bar are drawers, the wiki card a bottom sheet, and nothing is resizable.

title: The page bar holds the page's controls; a stage's tools float in the open space
statement: The page's controls and the stage's own controls MUST sit apart:
notes:
- **The page bar:** the top of the tab panel (`page-bar`), floating across the top of the stage between the nav and the side bar. At its left, the page's tabs (`role="tablist"`). At its right (`page-bar-actions`), the stage switch, a group labeled "Stage" whose buttons carry `aria-pressed`, then a thin divider, then the wiki card toggle and the side bar toggle at the far right. It MUST keep one fixed height (`--page-bar-height`), one line whatever it holds, the tabs scrolling sideways, so nothing below it moves. The header strip (`LA-V96-R09`) sits directly under it.
- **A stage's own tools:** what only one stage has (the graph's layout, depth, steps and filters; the trace's Gaps only filter; the ERD's key) MUST float inside the open space the panels leave, marked `data-stage-tools` with the side it sits on, never in the page bar and never as a header of its own above the stage.

A toggle that is on, a pressed stage or a shown panel, MUST use the one shared on look (`icon-button is-on`). Stage switches and layout actions MUST NOT appear anywhere else on the page.

On a phone the page bar is the same bar, compact (`page-bar is-compact`), under the shell's top bar: an "Open pages" button that opens the tabs as a sheet takes the tabs' place, the stage switch shows the three stages, and the wiki card and side bar toggles stay at the far right.

title: Motion is shared and optional
statement: Every transition and animation MUST take its time and easing from the shared tokens in `:root`: `--motion-speed` and `--motion-ease` for things that move or fade, and `--hover-speed` for hover. Each one MUST be turned off when the system asks for reduced motion, by a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` rule for the same selector or by applying only under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`. Animation in JS MUST read the same tokens and check `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')`, jumping straight to the end when it matches; `readMotion()` in `app/src/graph/motion.ts` does both. Motion only helps the eye follow a change: nothing may depend on it.

title: A row that leads to one record is one link
statement: A list row that leads to one record MUST be clickable anywhere on it, through one real link (`<a href>`) to that record, marked `row-link`, whose `::after` stretches over the whole row (`position: absolute; inset: 0`, the row being `position: relative`), as a card's title does (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R14`). A plain click navigates within the app; Cmd/Ctrl-click and middle-click open a new tab, because it is a real link. A row MUST have exactly one such link.
notes: Every other control in the row (a fold chevron, another record link such as "followed by UC01", a badge with a tooltip, a button) MUST sit above the stretched link, through one shared rule rather than one per control, so a click on it does what it did before. The row takes the link's hover (the `--hover-bg` tint, the title in steel) and its focus ring, while keyboard focus stays on the one link. A row's plain text cannot be drag-selected; that is accepted. A list that does not navigate, such as the side bar's facts, is not a row of this kind.

title: Every open thing has an address
statement: Anything a person can open MUST be reachable from the address bar or restorable from storage, so a reload brings it back as it was: a page and its stage are in the address (`/<id>?stage=erd`), and what the address cannot hold, such as the open tabs, which one is active, each tab's state and the session's settings, is kept in session or local storage and read back on load. A new kind of open thing (a tab, a stage, a panel state worth sharing) MUST come with a test that opens it, reloads the app at the same address and expects the same thing open. Storage is read with guards (`readPref`), so a missing or malformed value falls back to a default and never breaks the page.

title: Everything works by touch
statement: The app MUST work with a finger as well as a mouse:
notes:
- **Targets:** on a coarse pointer (`@media (pointer: coarse)`), every control's target MUST be at least 44 × 44 px (`--touch-target`): the control itself, or for a control drawn small inside a row or a node (a fold chevron, a tab's close button), a `::before` stretched around it, so its look does not change. Canvas nodes, laid out by the canvas and zoomed by a pinch, and whole cards are targets of their own size.
- **No hover-only paths:** no action or information MAY be reachable only by hover. A control a hover reveals MUST show always on a coarse pointer; a tooltip only repeats a name and keys the control already has, and opens on keyboard focus too; where a click opens something at once, a tap MUST first say what it is (`LA-V93-R02`).
- **No sideways scroll:** no page MAY scroll sideways at 320 px wide. No rule fixes a least width wider than the phone's content (288 px) outside a wide-screen media query; long IDs wrap; wide tables and code blocks scroll in their own box.

Proved in `app/test/standards.test.tsx` by reading the stylesheet and rendering the main pages on a phone; what jsdom cannot lay out is checked in a browser at 320 and 375 px.

title: Nothing jumps
statement: Nothing on screen MAY move unless the Reader moved it or it moves by a deliberate motion on the shared tokens (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R04`). In every scenario of the stability suite (`app/stability`, run by `npm --prefix app run test:stability`), the layout shifts that the step does not mean to make MUST add up to 0.01 or less, counting the shifts just after input that CLS leaves out, and the key elements of the page (the nav, the tab panel, the header strip, the wiki card, the stage's canvas, the side bar) MUST keep their boxes: they never move, jump back, or get thrown away and drawn anew. The causes that show in the source are checked without a browser too: every scroll box sets `scrollbar-gutter: stable`; a bar over the stage has a fixed block size or is one line cut with an ellipsis; a count or caption that changes is one text; a canvas stays mounted while its content changes and is fitted before its first paint; and what one part tells another (the graph telling the side bar what it connects, a stage telling the header strip its counts) arrives before paint. The causes and their fixes are listed in `notes/jitter-audit.md`.

title: Actions look like actions
statement: A standalone action MUST be the app's one `Button` component (`app/src/components/Button.tsx`), never a link dressed as text and never a button with a style of its own:
notes:
- **Ghost**, the default: no border or fill, padded, the `--hover-bg` tint on hover, the shared focus ring and an optional leading icon. "Expand all", "Clear filters", "Open the product overview", Cancel, Export and the desktop app's file actions are ghost buttons.
- **Primary**: filled with the accent, for the one main action of a form or dialog, such as Save.
- **Icon**: a square ghost button that holds only an icon and MUST be given an accessible name, such as the wiki card's collapse button or the side bar's toggle.

An action that goes to an address is a real link drawn as a button (`buttonClass()` on a router link, or `Button` with `href`), so Cmd/Ctrl-click still opens a new tab. On a coarse pointer a button is a 44 px target (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R07`).

Links stay links where they are navigation in context: inside prose (Markdown, or a sentence such as "See all products"), inside lists and rows (record references and the row links of `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R05`), in breadcrumbs, and in the navigation. Controls that are not standalone actions keep their own form: tabs, toggles in a group (the stage switch, the graph's depth), fold chevrons, the nav's rows and a card's title, stretched over its card (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R14`).

Proved in `app/test/standards.test.tsx` by rendering the main pages and reading the source.

title: Every page passes the accessibility audit
statement: Every page and state the app draws MUST pass the accessibility suite (`app/a11y`, run by `npm --prefix app run test:a11y`), with no finding:
notes:
- **The audit:** axe-core at WCAG 2.2 AA on the product, domain, record and group pages, each stage with the panels open and collapsed, Checks, Format and Appearance, quick find, the palette, the shortcuts sheet, a tooltip, the side bar and the phone's drawers and sheets, at 1440 px and 375 px, in the Lathe theme and High contrast, each in light and dark, and under reduced transparency.
- **What axe can't see**, walked by keyboard: Tab reaches every control and comes back round with no trap; the main tasks (open a record, switch stages, collapse the wiki card, re-center the graph, fold rows, show and hide the side bar, pick a theme) work by keyboard alone; focus stays on the page after a move and returns to the opener when a dialog or a sheet closes; the announcer says what changed.

A finding is fixed by its cause, across the app, and the cause and fix are listed in `notes/a11y-audit.md`. The suite runs on the stability suite's harness (Playwright with Chromium, one worker, a free port), and is run with it for every UI change.

title: Lathe stays within its performance budgets
statement: The app MUST stay within its performance budgets, measured on the production build in Chromium on the dev machine by the performance suite (`app/perf`, run by `npm --prefix app run test:perf` after the stability suite for a UI change), whose budgets are in `app/perf/budgets.ts`:

title: Every drawn box shows its name
statement: In every layout of the graph (Tree, Nested and Voronoi, and any layout added later), at every focus and depth, every box the app draws MUST show its name: its title in full, wrapped on whole words and never clipped, and its kind and ID line, at the box's fixed size in the map, however small it is on screen. A box is either drawn with its label or not drawn at all: off screen, under about 3 pixels, or past the drawing budget, a bar or its parent stands for it (`LA-EXP-DS10`). In every layout siblings are the same size with one text scale, the largest at which every sibling's whole label fits its box (`LA-EXP-DS06`), so every label fits its box by construction; a very small box has very small text, read by zooming in.
notes: It is proved at the unit level by a sweep over the repo's own specs (Lathe's and the Tool Library's), every layout, every domain, stage and folder focused at depths 1 to 3 in a 770 by 640 and a 1200 by 800 frame with the real camera (`app/test/graph/readable.test.ts`, in `npm --prefix app test`), and in the browser by the stability suite, which focuses each of Lathe's domains in each layout and checks every drawn box has visible title text.

title: Labels read in sentence case
statement: Every label, heading, button and field name the app shows MUST read in sentence case: only its first word, and any name of a thing, starts with a capital. No style MAY change a label's letter case word by word (CSS text-transform: capitalize); a label that wants a capital first letter MUST get it from its own text or ::first-letter.

title: A card has one primary action, taken by clicking anywhere on it
statement: Every card MUST have one primary action, opening what the card is or using it, whichever fits, and a click or tap anywhere on the card MUST take it: no card is a dead box. A card MUST be the app's one `Card` component (`app/src/shell/Card.tsx`), which requires its primary action, an address (`href`) or an action (`onActivate`), so a card without one does not compile. The card's title is that real link or button, and the title's `::after` stretches over the whole card (`position: absolute`, the card being `position: relative`), so the card has one tab stop and one accessible name, and Enter or Space takes its action.
notes:
Any other link or button in the card (a record named in its text, a theme's Duplicate and edit, Edit and Export, the tap card's let go) sits above the stretched title, through one shared rule, and does what it says. The whole card takes the title's hover ring (`--hover-ring`), its focus ring and the pointer. No element outside the component uses the card classes (`card`, `card-*`), and no stylesheet styles a card class the component does not set.

The cards and their primary actions:
- **Products page:** each product's card opens its product page.
- **Product page:** each business outcome's card opens the outcome; each domain's card opens the domain page.
- **Appearance page:** each theme's card uses the theme, and shows it as the one in use.
- **Trace view:** each card in an obligation's chain opens its record (a file's, the record that names it); the obligation's own card is marked as the current page.
- **Graph and ERD views by touch:** the card of a tapped node opens the node.

A problem row is a row of `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R05`, not a card, but it is never a dead box either: it opens its record, or its check's page when it names no record or the page is the record's own.

title: A stage with one folder shows its records directly
statement: A stage with only one folder MUST show that folder's records directly under the stage, with no folder level between: a domain's Use cases, which holds only capabilities, reads Use cases › Record authoring, not Use cases › Capabilities › Record authoring. A stage with two or more folders MUST keep them. It holds for every stage of every product, Shared included, decided per domain or product from the folders the folder model gives that stage (`LA-EXP-DS03`), empty ones that can start a branch counted, so the nav, the graph's tree, the stage's page, the domain and product pages, counts, keyboard walking and search all follow. The skipped folder MUST have no row, group or address of its own; whatever would link to it links to the stage. A stage whose one folder is empty shows as a stage with no records.

title: One breadcrumb, collapsed past three places
statement: Every trail of places above a page (the header strip's, the wiki card's, the phone's top bar's, and any other) MUST be the one `Breadcrumb` component (`app/src/components/Breadcrumb.tsx`). A trail of up to three places MUST show in full; a longer one MUST show its first place (the product), a "…" button and its last place (the immediate parent). The button MUST be labeled with how many levels it hides and open a menu of the hidden levels, each a link, reached by Tab and the arrow keys and closed by Escape (focus back on the button) or a click elsewhere. Each place is one line cut with an ellipsis, its whole name in its tooltip.

title: Every stage works on every focus
statement: Every stage MUST draw something useful for every focus, so the stage switch is never disabled, dimmed or hidden and a stage chosen stays chosen as the focus moves:
notes:
- **Graph:** the focus in the one map, as `LA-V93` says.
- **ERD:** the product's one map (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R19`), framed on the focus: a domain's region, an aggregate's boundary, an entity picked out in its aggregate; on any other record its nearest entity or aggregate above it, picked out in its domain (a table its entity), or its domain's region; for a Shared record (one in no domain) or a product, the whole map.
- **Trace:** the product's one map (`LA-PAT-APP-UX-R19`), framed on the focus: on an obligation its lane; on a record or group with obligations under it, its tree box or their lanes; on a design, build or test record that an obligation's chain holds, the first lane it belongs to, the record drawn as the focus in each; on a design, build or test record nothing traces to, an explicit untraced state ("Nothing traces to this record: it serves no requirement or rule.") and its row in the Untraced lane; on any other record (an entity, a value object, a term and similar), the nearest container the map draws.

The ERD's camera and fade are worked out by `erdFocus` (`app/src/erd/erd.ts`), the Trace's table by `traceShape` (`app/src/trace/chain.ts`) and its camera by `traceFocus` (`app/src/trace/lanes.ts`); no code gates a stage by the focus's kind.

title: Panels never crowd the page: they collapse in set order before anything gets unreadably narrow
statement: Every floating panel MUST keep a readable width, and the stage's open space at least 300 px between its gaps: the wiki card shrinks to 360 px and no further, and the nav and the side bar keep the width they were given. When the window can't hold every open panel at that width, panels MUST collapse for space in a set order, the side bar first, then the wiki card, then the nav to its rail, and reopen in reverse order as the window widens; the chat, the Reader's task at hand, never collapses for space. A collapse for space MUST NOT change the Reader's own open or closed choice, and MUST show: the collapsed panel's toggle wears a dashed ring, and its tooltip and name say it is collapsed to give the stage room. Opening such a panel holds it open, the next panel in the order giving way instead, until it would fit anyway or the Reader closes it. Titles MUST wrap on whole words, a word breaking only when it is longer than the line (`overflow-wrap: break-word`, as for an ID), and no text MAY use `word-break: break-all`.
notes: The rule is one function, `crowded` in `app/src/views/openSpace.ts`, from the window's width and the panels' widths: the shell (`App.tsx`) works it out, and the focus page reports its wiki card and side bar to it. The shell sets `--card-min` and `--stage-min` from the same numbers, so the card's CSS limits agree. With the chat open (400 px) and every panel at its default width, the side bar gives way at 1440 px, the wiki card too at 1280 px, and the nav as well at 1024 px; without the chat, 1440 px holds them all.

title: Every stage is one map: focusing moves the camera, nothing re-lays out
statement: Every canvas stage (the Graph, the ERD and the Trace) MUST lay a product out as one map, once per product and data change, and every box MUST keep its place and size whatever is focused or filtered and however deep the depth shows. Focusing a record MUST move only the camera, gliding on the shared motion to frame it (at once on a stage switch, which keeps the focus, and under reduced motion). A filter, the depth or a focus that shows only part of the map MUST fade the rest back to the focus fade's strength, never take it out or lay the map out again. Each frame MUST draw only what is in view.
notes: One code does it for every stage: `onePerData` (`app/src/graph/one-map.ts`) caches a product's layout by the spec's index, which is built anew on each data change; `keptFade` and `faintest` (`app/src/graph/fade.ts`) fade by place, a placed box's key, so a record a map draws twice can fade in one place and not the other; `frameRect` (`app/src/graph/camera.ts`) frames a rectangle of a map, and the graph's `frameOnMap` its tree; `useCameraGestures` (`app/src/graph/gestures.ts`) glides. The Graph's map is `graphMap` (`app/src/graph/map.ts`, LA-V93-R16), the Trace stage's `traceMap` (`app/src/trace/lanes.ts`, LA-V98-R12).
